observed_facts.fact: Authority interface and Service field are unexported and nil denies. Evidence currently checks only that RootWitnessSignature is nonempty; real verification is delegated to an unimplemented private verifier. Test verifier accepts a fixed literal.

Production control owns an opaque process-local DataRootLease before database open. Held checks the live handle. Borrow/ReturnBorrow can pin its lifetime and prevent Close while borrowed. Root pathname alone is insufficient proof of database identity.

ObserveControlAuthorityOwner measures current PID/creation/image, root and database file identities, checks accepted image hash and apps/control buildinfo. stableHash is a parameter; its acceptance anchor must not be caller-selected.

Existing native transport uses a 32-byte inherited HMAC capability and checks peer PID/creation/image plus named-pipe OS process identities. A same-user DACL alone does not identify the trusted parent. These are reusable patterns, not already an abandonment authority.
UpgradeLocal has fixed concrete protected-service verifier, explicit plan allowlist, alias/overlap checks and SQLite exclusive source ownership. It has no schema23-to24 plan.
Configuration plan is exact schema22-to23, pins releases and SQL, validates schema/inventory and protected references, makes backup, and migrates only an isolated restore target.

Generic restore always calls backupFence before migration. It revokes credentials, changes QUEUED to RECONCILING, rotates lease_token_hash, expires lease, bumps revision and appends events. Direct reuse invalidates candidate QUEUED/expected revision abandonment preconditions.

authority_design.recommended_boundary: A dedicated maintenance mode of the independently accepted apps/control binary, with no HTTP/native public listeners, no scheduler/coordinator launch and no provider setup. Ordinary CLI can request review, but cannot mint or inject capability.
construction: Keep preparedAbandonmentAuthority private and nil in New/NewCurrentMu and normal control startup. Never add an exported setter, configurable verifier callback, environment bypass, or a JSON field enabling authority.

Implement an internal leaf package for concrete Windows recovery authority, with no domain dependency. Domain can import its opaque concrete token type; apps/control can obtain that token only through its verified native bootstrap. An exported constructor must perform OS/cryptographic validation itself rather than accepting arbitrary expectedPeer, key or acceptedHash as the trust root.

Native acquisition independently verifies current accepted control image/build/source inventory against a frozen release anchor, current SID, data-root and database handle identities; holds DataRootLease (Borrow or equivalent full-operation lifetime lock), verifies exclusive SQLite owner in maintenance mode, and requires a private inherited peer-authenticated bootstrap. Bind the existing authenticated OWNER principal and project ownership, plus current explicit Root approval for this exact operation. OWNER authorization must be rechecked against the current DB in the CAS transaction; do not use old credentials or old LeaseToken as the recovery authority.

Reuse the drain channel security pattern but define a distinct abandonment protocol/purpose, fresh random key/nonce, strict frame limit, single operation and exact Run/Task/epoch/expected revisions/manifest/proof digest. Authenticate both peer PID+creation+accepted image through OS; same-SID DACL alone is insufficient. Do not reuse drain HMAC key or permit cross-protocol frames.

Trust anchor remains an explicit implementation gate: an independently accepted native Root/supervisor process must provision the one-use capability. Request JSON, a caller-selected public key, a file path, a backup encryption key or a publicly invokable helper that mints capabilities for arbitrary callers cannot be that anchor.

Token has unexported fields, no JSON/gob deserialization constructor, process instance binding, root+database file identity, exact proof/tuple, expiry and one-use state; zero value rejects. Factory in domain accepts only this concrete token and constructs the private concrete verifier after checking it against Service DB identity. Existing unexported interface can remain as test seam, but no production arbitrary implementation is accepted.

Do signature/key/OS evidence loading outside the DB write transaction with source read guards. Recheck immutable token identity, lifetime, data-root lease and exact proof digest under resourceWriteLock immediately before CAS. Hold file handles/guard and lease until commit/rollback. Avoid a verifier that opens another DB connection while the write lock is held.

Token use and proof insert must have defined crash semantics: rollback permits only the same still-valid in-process token; committed duplicate proof reads existing immutable tombstone without reopening authority to another tuple. Restart requires a fresh authorized maintenance session and verifies the stored proof rather than auto-replaying an action.

historical_path.proposal: Define a versioned HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_ADOPTION witness, signed now by the newly authenticated maintenance authority after independent review of pinned original receipts, source/binary/tool-IO lineage, and current DB CAS/absence checks. Record historical observer identity and observed-monotonic facts separately from current adopter identity/time. It is a current authorization to rely on bounded historical evidence, not a claim the old Python Root signed it. This is a concrete recovery route to implement and verify; absence of the old Root signature does not make recovery permanently impossible. Its schema, producer, signing time and authority scope must differ from the original unsigned historical receipt.
mandatory_gates: Current Root approval and current OWNER authorization are both bound through the closed trusted local Main/host composition and authenticated native bootstrap; the public caller cannot select its signer/trust anchor. Authorize exactly one historical trial adoption with exact source/binary/evidence pins.
Bind exact raw SHA256+size of whole clock, once, GO grant, original authority, contract/probe, both invocation/stdstreams, complete lifecycle/closure, source/binary and original tool IO.
Validate all identity duplicates, held-before-resume markers, native actual exit and primary-exit consistency, active0/errors[], duplicate/producer close; preserve original diagnostic failure.

Historical evidence alone cannot prove absence of later activity. Under exclusive data-root and DB lock recheck current exact Run/Task/dispatch, epoch/revisions, marker, sealed preparation baseline, accounting/effects/queue. Any new footprint or provenance gap rejects.

Implement the new adoption schema explicitly and retain old v1 contemporaneous semantics. Preserve absent historical signature/absolute close UTC as absent. Sign only the current adoption decision and current exclusive-state verification; do not fill absent old facts.

authority_design.signing: Use a purpose-separated asymmetric signature for durable reviewable adoption evidence, with key identity/public trust anchor enrolled outside the request; ephemeral HMAC is appropriate for the private transport but does not independently establish long-term signed origin. Define payload as fixed typed/versioned bytes excluding the signature itself, plus raw evidence digests. Encode FILETIME/monotonic identities losslessly as typed decimal strings in the new witness, without altering original receipts or global canonical semantics.
closed_local_flow: Reviewed native Root/supervisor receives the current operation approval in its trusted local composition and authenticates the current OWNER principal with existing authorization logic; a JSON approved=true is not sufficient.

Root starts the accepted maintenance control/host process with an inherited private bootstrap whose OS peer PID, birth time and accepted binary/source inventory are pinned. No HTTP or ordinary native public method receives the token.

Maintenance process acquires and holds the original DataRootLease and exact root/DB file handles, obtains SQLite exclusive ownership, verifies all immutable old receipt/source/binary pins and recorded closed Jobs without reopening old PIDs.

Under the same domain write lock used by launch, verify current OWNER/project authorization, exact PREPARED dispatch with no worker identity/journal, exact Run/Task/epoch/revisions/marker/profile baseline, and absence of disallowed model/runtime/queue/accounting footprints.

Construct and sign the new current-adoption witness with current producer, current UTC, current native owner identity, original evidence digest set, current state digest/CAS tuple, action, purpose and one-use nonce. The native signature proves only this current adoption and authorization.

Private domain factory binds the opaque token to that service/DB and witness. Abandonment transaction rechecks the tuple and token lifetime and writes the immutable abandonment proof plus the defined Run/Task FAILED transition atomically; no fake observation, ledger release or financial closure.
Record actual execution and closure separately. Any change after preview requires renewed evidence review/CAS, never reset old once/clock or reuse old runtime capability.

migration_design.recommended_plan: A new fixed schema23-to24-prepared-abandonment-v1 maintenance plan, distinct from every historical upgrade ID.
phases: Compile and independently verify accepted source23 and target24 release inventories/binaries. Inventory requires exact numbered1..23 and1..24, existing frozen contract/additive hashes, and exact0024 bytes. Build expected source/target schema hashes on disposable test DBs only during implementation validation.

Enter explicitly authorized offline maintenance: do not start HTTP, public native listeners, coordinator Recover, scheduler or model transports. Hold original DataRootLease and SQLite EXCLUSIVE connection for backup through migration result; validate plain paths and handle identities and all original byte pins. Other owners/processes must cause bounded failure.

Create encrypted matching-program schema23 backup using existing backup integrity/protected-reference policy. A protected service unavailable or reference mismatch remains a blocker; do not export protected payloads or weaken checks. Keep encryption key separate and never log it.

Restore the complete matching schema23 backup into an unpublished isolated destination using existing MAC/decryption, protected-reference, schema/history validation and normal recovery fencing. Add only the fixed23-to24 plan hook. Record the exact restoration-only changes (credential revocation, QUEUED-to-RECONCILING, lease/revision/events and relocation/acceptance effects). These changes are confined to this isolated copy.

Within the isolated copy, establish a post-restore/pre-DDL baseline, execute exactly the pinned0024, and require every pre-existing business row unchanged from that baseline; only schema_migrations adds24, new proof table is empty and intended triggers are added. Preserve the full source-to-restored delta so no restoration effect is misreported as a migration effect. Run integrity/FK, trigger and rollback checks. The rehearsal performs no abandonment or provider execution.

After reviewed rehearsal and explicit production migration approval, retain or reacquire original-root exclusive ownership, then verify its current schema23/logical hashes and all business rows still equal the reviewed pre-backup source. In one original-DB transaction execute the same pinned0024/add24 and verify all original business rows are unchanged, table empty, exact target schema, integrity/FK. Do not call restore/backupFence on the original root and do not copy restored rows back. Commit only after all checks pass.

Write an immutable migration receipt with source/target schema+logical hashes, backup/rehearsal refs, migration/program pins and original process/result evidence. On interrupted commit, inspect durable version/schema/receipt under exclusive ownership; do not automatically repeat or edit old rows. Once committed, rollback strategy is a separately authorized restoration of the preserved backup, not deleting migration/proof records.

Run abandonment later as a distinct independently authorized domain operation under the concrete capability, with fresh current expected revisions and unchanged historical once/clock/failure lineage. Do not combine schema migration with Run FAILED or proof creation. Resume normal serving only after separate single-writer cutover/review.
migration_design.why_same_root: Production schema-only in-place DDL preserves original QUEUED/Task RUNNING/dispatch PREPARED, all lease/auth/revision/history/ledger rows and original root/DB identity.
